pairs.difference: A: an orange planet with a pure magenta band, and the ring is a warm cream/peach set against a saturated cyan field. Every mass is a pure hue, there is no muted local color, and shadow chroma rises (1.26) instead of falling. B: yellow fins and purple foot pockets on a very loud purple field. The background chroma (0.24) is above the real range, but the fins' shadows drop toward muted violet the way the real cards do. Both cards are loud, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Give the planet a muted, dusty orange with soft brownish shadows. Make the ring a light neutral grey-beige rather than peach cream. Tone the stripe down to a dull rose.

pairs.difference: A: a red booth, a blue/white/red target and a brown bear under warm lamp light. That is many hue families with believable local colors. B: a magenta tray with blue ice on a wood table and a cyan sunburst. Its hues are varied and its wood is natural brown. Neither card shows the cream-white or single-hue drift.

A: a pure red rocket on a cyan sunburst. The silver body takes on the cyan of the background in the lens and reads as a light blue mass, not a neutral grey. The card has only two hue families (1.99, below the real range). B: a yellow submarine on a green field with copper portholes and grey fins. That makes three related families, and its shadows turn to a darker ochre.
pairs.fix: Paint the rocket body a neutral steel grey with slightly cool grey shadows, not blue-tinted. Add a small second accent, such as a warm yellow flame and a dark navy nozzle, so the card is not just red and cyan.

pairs.difference: A: the 'white' robot reads as cream-yellow in the lens because the warm wall bleeds over the whole body (subject chroma 0.017, warm share 0.999). The floor is a warm grey, and only a tiny red dot carries any accent. This is the same cream-white drift as the generated computers in the lessons. B: red gloves on a blue plank wall and orange wood. The local colors are believable, and the shadows go to a deep crimson.
pairs.fix: Paint the robot a cool, clean white with light blue-grey shadows that do not pick up the yellow wall. Give it one clear color accent, such as blue eyes or a teal chest panel.

pairs.difference: B is the real computer card from the lessons: a neutral grey-white plastic case with cool grey shadows against an orange field. A: a lime alien on hot magenta. Both are pure complementary hues at full chroma, the metal floor goes pink-violet, and nothing neutral rests the eye.
pairs.fix: Make the alien a softer leaf green with darker green shadows. Make the backdrop a muted dusty pink. Make the floor a neutral steel grey, not pink.

pairs.difference: A: a green slide, a blue ladder and a yellow deck on a pink wavy wall, with a white tile pool. That is several families with clear roles. B: a beach ball with red, blue, green and white panels on warm sand. Its local colors are believable, and the shadows go to violet and olive rather than orange. Both sit inside the real range.

B: the whole card is one violet family. The silver pod, the floor and the walls all collapse into lavender/purple, with only cyan neon and small orange dots (hue families 2.8, warm share 0.05). The metal has no neutral grey of its own. A: a red bus against a blue sky, cream clouds and pink buildings. That is several local colors, with neutral grey asphalt.
pairs.fix: Paint the pod a neutral silver-grey with grey shadows. Bring in a contrasting warm wall or floor color so the scene is not all purple, and keep the cyan glow as the single accent.

pairs.difference: B: a dead-grey console on a grey metal shelf (subject chroma 0.03, far below the real minimum of 0.07) against a flat orange field. The only color on the object is the small red buttons. A: a blue machine on a magenta field with multicolored cans. That gives a clear hue role for the hero against the background.
pairs.fix: Give the console a colored body, such as a saturated teal or blue painted metal with grey trim. Keep the red buttons as the accent.

pairs.difference: B: the white helmet shell is cream-peach, the visor is amber-orange, and the background is orange (warm share 0.98). The whole card is pulled into one warm family, with a thin blue stripe as the only relief. This is the same cream-white drift as the generated lesson cards. A: a tan jacket with an orange collar and a green sash on a green field. The local colors are natural, and the shadows go to brown.
pairs.fix: Paint the helmet a clean, cool white with light blue-grey shadows. Make the visor dark smoky blue with a reflection, so the helmet stands apart from the orange background.

pairs.difference: A: an almost colorless card. The rover is white-grey with grey wheels on grey moon dust under a blue sky (subject chroma 0.02, warm share 0.008), and only a small yellow dish adds color. B: an orange boat and dock on turquoise water with green lily pads. The hero and background are complements, the wood is natural, and the shadows are a rich red-brown.
pairs.fix: Give the rover a colored body, such as orange or red panels with white trim. Warm the moon ground slightly toward a beige-grey so the card has more than one hue family.

pairs.difference: B: the silver saucer and blue dome sit on a violet field, and in the lens the whole object merges into the background violet (hue families 1.26). The grey metal picks up purple, and only the small orange lights break it. A: a yellow-orange player against violet, with white earbuds. The hero hue contrasts with the background.
pairs.fix: Paint the saucer a neutral or warm steel grey that stays separate from the purple background. Make the dome a clear cyan, and keep the orange lights as the accent.

pairs.difference: A: the whole card is blue, with blue solar panels, a blue-white station, blue space and a blue planet (hue families 1.39, warm share 0.002). The only accent is a tiny red bulb, and the grey metal goes blue in the lens. B: a tiki bar with brown thatch, teal water, green stools, a yellow pineapple and pink drinks. That is many local colors with natural wood browns.
pairs.fix: Make the station body a warm white with gold/orange foil panels, and use dark navy solar panels with a slight purple sheen. Keep the planet's green land and white clouds so the card is not all blue.

pattern: Generated cards break in two ways on color. In the first, the card collapses into one hue family: grey or white metal takes on the background color (silver turns cyan, violet or blue), so the hero merges with the field (p03, p07, p11, p12). In the second, the warm background floods the 'white' surfaces, which turn cream or peach (robot, helmet), as with the cream computers in the lessons. The opposite failure also appears: a nearly colorless grey hero with no local color (control panel, moon rover). Real cards keep neutral greys and cool whites as their own masses, give the hero a hue that contrasts with the background, and carry three or more believable local colors.
